This is the "hide it but keep it" I meant, and it's clearly a different thing from deleting — which is what I wanted. Archiving the potato bookmark took it out of my everyday collection, but it wasn't gone; it was sitting safely under Archived, still with its title and description intact, and Restore brought it right back. That's the reversible tuck-away I was picturing, as opposed to the permanent delete with its scary warning.

The behavior you assumed matches what I mean: while something's archived it should stay out of my normal list and out of my everyday searching, so it's not cluttering me up — but it keeps everything about itself, its labels and its read-later flag included, so that when I restore it, it comes back exactly as it was, not stripped down. Good.

This is right. What's next?
